patch.value: The release workflow falls back to an unattested npm publish and exits zero

value.author: claude
value.text:
The release workflow ended its publish retry loop with an unattested fallback:
publish_without_provenance() {
echo "::warning::Falling back to publish WITHOUT --provenance after repeated 404 from npm registry."
npm publish --access public --ignore-scripts
}
...
echo "::warning::All ${max_attempts} provenance publish attempts failed; trying once without provenance."
if publish_without_provenance; then echo "Published without provenance."; exit 0; fi
So after three failed attested attempts the job published an artifact nobody can trace back to this workflow and exited 0. The only trace was a ::warning:: in the log of a run that otherwise looked like a healthy release, and this repository has a Daily Release, so it could fire unattended.
An unattested version is worse than no release: a release can be retried, but a published version number cannot be reused, so the untraceable artifact stays on the registry under the version the attested one should have had.
Removed the fallback function and the block that called it. The registry re-read that followed it is kept, because npm can accept a publish and still report an error; with the fallback gone, a version that is present is one npm accepted from an attested attempt. The job now fails loudly instead.
This is the change 17 other packages already carry, from the pm-ops reference. This package was not in that wave and, unlike those 17, has no scripts/verify-release-publish-attestation.ts to catch a regression. Rather than vendor an eighteenth copy of that 400-line verifier — the vendoring is itself the defect recorded in the companion as pm-cli-website-bunt — this adds a focused test that reads the workflow, joins line continuations first so a split invocation is not read as a flagless fragment, and asserts that every npm publish it finds carries --provenance and none disables it. It also asserts the scan found at least one publish, so the test cannot pass by looking in the wrong place.
Revert-proof observed: restoring the fallback fails the test with "every publish must enable --provenance, but this one does not: npm publish --access public --ignore-scripts".
Found while checking which packages carry the shared shell-command scanner; the three without it turned out to be the three with no attestation gate at all. Companion item pm-cli-website-e3pl records the fleet view, including pm-changelog, which does not fall back but also has no gate.
